searches.reason: Resolve the execution-audit bottleneck before interpreting history interventions. Seek reference-based tests that distinguish recurrent padding effects, readout or adapter errors, and floating-point batch variation. The observed final-feature discrepancies alongside zero reported candidate-score discrepancies warrant tracing the complete scoring path. Calibrate checks against repeated execution and ranking stability rather than simply relaxing tolerances; preserve the trained checkpoint’s semantics.

searches.reason: Move beyond whether shuffling changes recommendations to identifying where historical information is lost or becomes irrelevant to scores. Seek bounded, inference-only interventions on the existing GRU’s hidden states and gates, with matched controls and target-versus-competitor score attribution. These could distinguish memory decay from an insensitive output projection without fitting additional predictors. Treat findings as conditional model mechanisms, not causal user intent or generalization evidence.

searches.reason: Translate qualitative complaints into auditable recommendation evidence. Seek annotation protocols linking actual feedback to supporting history and title/description spans, separating explicit specification conflicts, functional similarity, and insufficient information. Validate with independently annotated examples, agreement and abstention rates; do not infer ownership, compatibility, unmet need, or user traits from similarity alone. Keep the twenty simulator users descriptive and official macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion.
